'''Oded Schramm''' ({{langx|he|עודד שרם}}; December 10, 1961&nbsp;– September 1, 2008) was an Israeli-American mathematician known for the invention of the [[Schramm–Loewner evolution]] (SLE) and for working at the intersection of [[conformal field theory]] and [[probability theory]].<ref>{{cite web| title = Clay Mathematics Institute| access-date = 2008-09-12| url = http://www.claymath.org/research_award/Schramm/| archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080829143806/http://www.claymath.org./research_award/Schramm/| archive-date = 2008-08-29| url-status = dead}}</ref><ref>{{citation|first=Gregory F.|last=Lawler|author-link=Greg Lawler|series=Mathematical Surveys and Monographs|volume=114|title=Conformally Invariant Processes in the Plane|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|year=2005|isbn=0-8218-3677-3|location=Providence, RI|mr=2129588}}</ref>

==Biography==
Schramm was born in [[Jerusalem]].<ref name="Chang_2008_09_10"/> His father, Michael Schramm, was a biochemistry professor at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].

He attended Hebrew University, where he received his [[bachelor's degree]] in mathematics and computer science in 1986 and his master's degree in 1987, under the supervision of [[Gil Kalai]].  He then received his PhD from [[Princeton University]] in 1990 under the supervision of [[William Thurston]].

After receiving his doctorate, he worked for two years at the [[University of California, San Diego]], and then had a permanent position at the [[Weizmann Institute]] from 1992 to 1999.  In 1999 he moved to the Theory Group at [[Microsoft Research]] in [[Redmond, Washington]], where he remained for the rest of his life.

He and his wife had two children, Tselil and Pele.<ref name="Chang_2008_09_10"/> Tselil is an assistant professor of statistics at Stanford University.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://tselilschramm.org/ |title=Tselil Schramm |publisher=Tselil Schramm |date= |accessdate=2022-09-04}}</ref>

On September 1, 2008, Schramm fell to his death while [[scrambling]] [[Guye Peak]], north of [[Snoqualmie Pass]] in [[Washington (state)|Washington]].<ref name="Chang_2008_09_10">{{citation
 | last = Chang | first = Kenneth
 | date = September 10, 2008
 | journal = [[New York Times]]
 | title = Oded Schramm, 46, Mathematician, Is Dead
 | url = https://www.nytimes.com/2008/09/11/science/11schramm.html}}</ref><ref>{{citation
 | last = Gutierrez | first = Scott
 | date = September 3, 2008
 | journal = [[Seattle Post-Intelligencer]]
 | title = Rescuers recover hiker's body near Cascades' Guye Peak
 | url = http://www.seattlepi.com/local/377577_hiker04.html}}</ref><ref>{{citation
 |date        = September 4, 2008
 |journal     = [[Seattle Times]]
 |title       = Accomplished Microsoft mathematician died in hiking accident
 |url         = http://blog.seattletimes.nwsource.com/techtracks/2008/09/04/accomplished_microsoft_mathematician_died_in_hikin.html
 |url-status     = dead
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20080922113114/http://blog.seattletimes.nwsource.com/techtracks/2008/09/04/accomplished_microsoft_mathematician_died_in_hikin.html
 |archive-date = September 22, 2008
}}</ref>

==Research==
[[Image:circleRiemannMap1.svg|right|thumb|Illustration by Schramm of an approximate [[conformal map]] using the [[circle packing theorem]].]]
A constant theme in Schramm's research was the exploration of relations between discrete models and their continuous scaling limits, which for a number of models turn out to be [[conformally invariant]].

Schramm's most significant contribution was the invention of [[Schramm–Loewner evolution]], a tool which has paved the way for mathematical proofs of conjectured scaling limit relations<ref>{{citation|title=Critical percolation in finite geometries|first=John|last= Cardy|author-link=John Cardy|year= 1992| journal=J. Phys. A: Math. Gen.|volume= 25|pages= L201–L206|url=http://www.iop.org/EJ/abstract/0305-4470/25/4/009/|doi=10.1088/0305-4470/25/4/009|bibcode=1992JPhA...25L.201C|arxiv = hep-th/9111026|issue=4|mr=1151081|s2cid=16037415}}</ref><ref>{{citation |url=http://www.iop.org/EJ/article/0305-4470/35/41/102/a241l2.html|first=John|last=Cardy|author-link=John Cardy|journal=J. Phys. A: Math. Gen.|volume= 35 |pages= L565–L572|year=2002|title=Crossing formulae for critical percolation in an annulus |doi=10.1088/0305-4470/35/41/102 |issue=41|mr=1946958|arxiv=math-ph/0208019|bibcode=2002math.ph...8019C|s2cid=119655247}}</ref> on models from [[statistical mechanics]] such as [[self-avoiding walk|self-avoiding random walk]] and [[percolation]]. This technique has had a profound impact on the field.<ref name="Chang_2008_09_10"/><ref name="google scholar"/>  It has been recognized by many awards to Schramm and others, including a [[Fields Medal]] to [[Wendelin Werner]], who was one of Schramm's principal collaborators, along with [[Gregory Lawler]]. ''[[The New York Times]]'' wrote in his obituary:<ref name="Chang_2008_09_10"/>

{{blockquote|If Dr. Schramm had been born three weeks and a day later, he would almost certainly have been one of the winners of the Fields Medal, perhaps the highest honor in mathematics, in 2002.}}

Schramm's doctorate<ref name="phd">{{citation | title=Combinatorically Prescribed Packings and Applications to Conformal and Quasiconformal Maps|year=2007|first=Oded|last=Schramm|arxiv=0709.0710|bibcode = 2007PhDT.......441S | volume=0709 | page=710 }}. Modified version of Schramm's Ph.D. thesis from 1990.</ref> was in [[complex analysis]], but he made contributions in many other areas of pure mathematics, although self-taught in those areas. Frequently he would prove a result by himself before reading the literature to obtain an appropriate credit. Often his proof was original or more elegant than the original.<ref name="Daily_Telegraph">{{citation
 | date = September 19, 2008
 | journal = [[Daily Telegraph]]
 | title = Mathematician who made a significant contribution to the study of probability and fractals
 | url = https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/2984516/Oded-Schramm.html}}</ref>

Besides conformally invariant planar processes and SLE, he made fundamental contributions to several topics:<ref name="google scholar">{{cite web | title = Oded Schramm's publications on Google Scholar | url = https://scholar.google.com/scholar?hl=en&lr=&q=Oded+Schramm}}</ref>

* The [[circle packing theorem]] and discrete [[conformal geometry]].
* Embeddings of [[Gromov hyperbolic space]]s.
* [[Percolation theory|Percolation]], [[uniform spanning tree|uniform]] and [[minimal spanning tree|minimal]] spanning trees and forests, [[harmonic function]]s on [[Cayley graph]]s of infinite finitely generated groups (especially [[amenable group|non-amenable groups]]) and the [[Hyperbolic geometry|hyperbolic plane]].
* Limits of sequences of finite [[Graph (discrete mathematics)|graphs]].
* Noise sensitivity of [[Boolean function]]s, with applications to dynamical percolation.
* Random turn games (e.g. random turn [[hex (board game)|hex]]) and the [[infinity Laplacian]] equation.
* [[Random permutation]]s.

==Awards and honors==
*[[Erdős Prize]] (1996)<ref>{{citation|url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Honours/Anna_and_Lajos_Erdos_Prize/|title=The Anna and Lajos Erdős Prize in Mathematics|work=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics Archive]]|publisher=[[University of St Andrews]]|access-date=2025-06-04}}</ref>
*[[Salem Prize]] (2001)<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.ams.org/notices/200108/people.pdf|title=Schramm and Smirnov Awarded 2001 Salem Prize|last=Kehoe|first=Elaine|journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]]|volume=48|year=2001|issue=8|page=831}}</ref>
*[[Clay Research Award]] (2002),<ref name="ClayMathematics">{{cite web|url=http://www.claymath.org/research_award/Schramm/|title=Clay Research Award citation: Oded Schramm|publisher=[[Clay Mathematics Institute]]|access-date=2008-09-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080829143806/http://www.claymath.org./research_award/Schramm/|archive-date=2008-08-29|url-status=dead}}</ref> for his ''work in combining analytic power with geometric insight in the field of random walks, percolation, and probability theory in general, especially for formulating stochastic Loewner evolution. His work opens new doors and reinvigorates research in these fields.'' <ref name="ClayMathematics"/>
*[[Loève Prize]] (2003)
*[[Poincaré Prize|Henri Poincaré Prize]] (2003),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iamp.org/poincare/|title=The Henri Poincaré Prize|publisher=[[International Association of Mathematical Physics]]|access-date=2008-09-04}}</ref> ''For his contributions to discrete conformal geometry, where he discovered new classes of circle patterns described by integrable systems and proved the ultimate results on convergence to the corresponding conformal mappings, and for the discovery of the Stochastic Loewner Process as a candidate for scaling limits in two dimensional statistical mechanics.''<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.iamp.org/poincare/os03-laud.pdf|title=Henri Poincaré Prize of the IAMP|publisher=[[International Association of Mathematical Physics]]}}</ref>
*[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]] [[Pólya Prize (SIAM)|George Pólya Prize]] (2006),<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/publicawareness/panews.php?id=967|title=Gregory F. Lawler, Oded Schramm and Wendelin Werner receive George Polya Prize in Boston|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]]|date=2006-04-20|access-date=2008-09-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090504060612/http://www.siam.org/publicawareness/panews.php?id=967|archive-date=2009-05-04|url-status=dead}}</ref> with [[Gregory Lawler]] and [[Wendelin Werner]], for ''groundbreaking work on the development and application of stochastic Loewner evolution (SLE).  Of particular note is the rigorous establishment of the existence and conformal invariance of critical scaling limits of a number of 2D lattice models arising in statistical physics.'' <ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/2006_luncheon.php|title=2006 Prizes and Awards Luncheon&nbsp;– SIAM Annual Meeting&nbsp;– July 11, 2006|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]]}}</ref>
*[[Ostrowski Prize]] (2007)
* Elected in 2008 as a foreign member of the [[Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences]].<ref>{{cite web| title = About Microsoft Research: Awards| access-date = 2008-09-12| url = http://research.microsoft.com/aboutmsr/pastpresentfuture/awards.aspx|publisher=[[Microsoft]]}}</ref>
